prompt: The migration patterns of Arctic birds
text:
, the migration of Arctic sea urchins and their migratory habits have not been well understood. As the Arctic ice sheets retreated, other factors included increased salinity and ocean acidification, and by 2100 increased Arctic temperatures and carbon footprints. This new study shows that while the amount of freshwater in the Arctic became more variable, the numbers of Arctic birds and sea urchins continued their migratory patterns, which are not fully accounted for in these new data.

"Our results show that we have been able to investigate the spatial migratory habitat of Arctic sea urchins at high resolution into the mid-western U.S. [Northwest], as well as to analyze migratory routes, the geographical dispersal of Arctic sea urchins from Greenland back to the west and the migration patterns of Arctic sea urchins to the North Carolina coast," said Dr. Robert Heger from the University of Illinois at Chicago. "Most of us know nothing about migratory patterns yet, but this is the first time a group of Arctic sea urchins has managed to establish a consistent pattern so precisely to capture our knowledge."

Dr. Heger, associate professor of sociology at the University of Massachusetts, Amherst, and M. I. Chumley of M.I.T.S. helped organize the study.
